rationale: The plan correctly refuses to re-run DESeq2 and goes straight to a preranked hallmark GSEA on the full 12,000-gene list, naming the ranking metric (signed Wald statistic, with sign(log2FC)*-log10(p) as the stated fallback) and explicitly rejecting log2FC-only ranking and any restriction to significant genes, which is exactly the reference behaviour; it also names the human hallmark collection with an MSigDB version, fixes a seed, applies BH across all 50 sets, and reports leading edges annotated with per-gene stats. QC is dataset-specific rather than generic: library sizes with sample_01's ratio to the median, VST/log-CPM PCA labelled by condition and depth, plus internal coherence checks on the supplied table (column names, p-histogram, padj monotonicity, NA-padj vs baseMean) and symbol-space overlap with the counts. Filtering is handled sensibly by refusing a second aggressive filter on an already-filtered 12k matrix and dropping only NA ranking values; normalization is only relevant for PCA and the ssGSEA step, and library-size normalization is stated there. Weaknesses are minor: the gene-set size window is only half-specified (sets under 15 are flagged as underpowered rather than a stated 15-500 filter), the permutation scheme/count is left as 'permutation- or multilevel-based', and tool versions (fgsea/gseapy) are not committed to in the report. The leave-one-out ssGSEA robustness step is scope beyond the reference but is justified for n=6 with a low-depth library and does not displace the preranked analysis.
